outcome: Late presentation of developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) beyond 12 months of age
cohort: Fifty-four children with typical DDH and frank hip dislocation, whose treatment was delayed for 12 months or more, were included in the study.
finding: Diagnostic delay was the most common reason for late presentation of DDH, primarily attributed to physician-related factors (e.g., inadequate hip screening at birth) and family/social issues (e.g., unawareness of the disorder).
